8. Economics against a competent attachment
Candidate service cost

The model uses exactly the requested application scale:

100 installed interfaces.
100 accepted services/interface/year.
Ten years and 8% real discounting.
$80/MWh electricity.
$40/h loaded labor.

Discounted accepted services total approximately 67,101.

The hypothetical manufacturing case assumes 10,000 receiver pairs/year and 85% yield. It includes carriers, spring sheets, patterned terminals, masks, seals, counter grid, reservoir, couplers, assembly, QA, tooling and installation.

The resulting introduced installed pair price is $416.71.

Three spares, an $18,000 service cart, $2,500 unloading fixture, $6,000 proof/metrology fixture and $30,000 application qualification produce approximately $99,421 initial cash, before the allocated robot.

Active cartridges are renewed at year five at approximately $302/pair, under an unqualified life of 500 accepted services. Pump/seal and electronic renewal are separately charged.

The model also pays:

Rejected attempts and recovery.
Calibration and inspection.
Chemical assays and waste collection.
Cleaning, filters and variable waste.
Additional chemical-cart downtime.
Robot and human service.
Retirement.

The resulting cost is $2.77 per potential accepted service.

Mechanical reference

The stronger practical reference is a prepared steel attachment with:

Two 49 × 49 mm adapters.
One recessed captive M5 screw with approximately 3 kN calibrated preload.
Two 4 mm hardened shear keys at ±15 mm.
Paid receiver bores, driver access and unloading support.
Inspection, lubrication, rejected attempts and finite screw/bush renewal.

A conservative screen putting the entire 1000 N shear load through one 4 mm pin gives approximately 79.6 MPa nominal pin shear and 83.3 MPa bearing at 3 mm engagement. Bolt load, face preload, prying, receiver stiffness and release after unloading still require matched assembly qualification.

This is not a claim that an unspecified catalog latch automatically certifies the whole joint. It is a construction from mature, inexpensive components. As additional evidence of strong competition, Howmet lists a 900 N working load for an individual Camloc 2600-series fastener.
